script: دل کے آئینے میں ہے تصویرِ یار
romanized: Dil ke aaine mein hai tasveer-e-yaar
translation: In the mirror of the heart lies the beloved's image
interpretations: The lover sees only the beloved whenever they look inward — a statement of total devotion
The heart itself has become a reflective surface — love has transformed the self into pure receptivity
The image is trapped inside — the beloved is gone but their presence is permanently etched in memory
author: Mir Taqi Mir

script: ہزاروں خواہشیں ایسی کہ ہر خواہش پہ دم نکلے
romanized: Hazaron khwahishen aisi ke har khwahish pe dam nikle
translation: Thousands of desires, such that each desire takes a breath away
interpretations: The sheer volume of unfulfilled longing is itself a form of slow death — desire as consumption
Each desire is so intense it feels life-threatening — hyperbole expressing the overwhelming nature of want
The speaker is overwhelmed not by one love but by the multiplicity of desires pulling in all directions simultaneously
author: Mirza Ghalib

script: No man is an island, entire of itself
romanized: No man is an island, entire of itself
translation: No man is an island, entire of itself
interpretations: Human beings are fundamentally interconnected — isolation is an illusion and every person's existence affects others
The self is not self-sufficient — we are constituted by our relationships and without them we are incomplete
A political statement — individual sovereignty is a myth, community and collective responsibility are the truth of human existence
author: John Donne

script: Because I could not stop for Death, He kindly stopped for me
romanized: Because I could not stop for Death, He kindly stopped for me
translation: Because I could not stop for Death, He kindly stopped for me
interpretations: Death is personified as a gentleman — the poem subverts fear of death by making it feel like a polite social encounter
The speaker was too busy living to think about death — death came anyway, indifferent to human plans
Ironic reading — death is not kind at all, the word kindly drips with dark irony, the carriage is a hearse
author: Emily Dickinson

script: मैं नीर भरी दुख की बदली
romanized: Main neer bhari dukh ki badli
translation: I am a cloud filled with the water of sorrow
interpretations: The poet identifies herself as a rain cloud — heavy with grief, destined to pour and then disappear
Sorrow is not a burden but a fullness — the cloud is not broken, it is complete, ready to give
A feminist reading — the woman is always expected to hold grief silently and release it for others while herself dissolving
author: Mahadevi Varma

translation: For the wise, time passes in the delight of poetry and learning
interpretations: Poetry and scholarship are the highest pleasures — time spent in them is time well spent
The wise do not feel time passing because they are absorbed in something larger than themselves
A subtle critique — only the wise use time this way, implying most people waste it on lesser things
author: Traditional

translation: Every place is my hometown, every person is my kin
interpretations: A radical statement of universal belonging — the poet refuses all boundaries of nation, caste, and community
Born of exile or displacement — when you have lost your home, everywhere becomes home and everyone becomes family
A philosophical stance — attachment to place and people is the root of suffering, releasing it brings universal love
author: Kaniyan Pungundranar

translation: Desires are not achieved through mere wishing
interpretations: A call to action — wishing is passive, achievement requires struggle and sacrifice
A meditation on fate — some things cannot be obtained no matter how hard you try, wishing reveals this gap
A critique of passive spirituality — even in devotion, action is required, not just prayer
author: Al-Mutanabbi
